title: Most Colon Grading Mistakes Are Neighbors: Adjacent-Grade Error Shares and Grade-3 Recall on Public Histopathology Embeddings
content: Colon histology computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) papers often lead with pooled grading accuracy. That number mixes easy majority-class hits with minority-class misses and treats a Grade 1↔Grade 2 swap as interchangeable with calling poorly differentiated cancer well differentiated. This preprint recomputes stratified five-fold support-vector grading on 560 public colorectal cancer patches with frozen ResNet50 embeddings (Grade 1 n=251, Grade 2 n=210, Grade 3 n=99). Cross-validated accuracy is 73.6% ± 2.9% and macro-F1 is 0.705, but Grade 3 recall is only 0.475. Of 148 residual mistakes, 119 (80.4%) are adjacent-grade swaps; 29 (19.6%) jump from Grade 3 to Grade 1. A published soft-voting ensemble confusion matrix shows the same structure: 86.0% of errors remain adjacent. We treat that adjacent share as the checkable claim—not a new leaderboard—and argue that Grade 3 recall and adjacent versus non-adjacent error counts should be reported before pooled accuracy is read as a deployment summary. Embedding protocol and ensemble confusion-matrix anchors follow a published two-stage colon pipeline; no new patients were enrolled.
